title: Advanced Wireframe Overlay with Depth-Tested Edges and Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an advanced wireframe overlay system with depth-tested edges and a scoring system.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Add a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 1.0 and an ambient light with intensity 0.3.
- Set the renderer background to #1a1a2e.
- The scene contains exactly 5 geometric objects arranged in a circle of radius 4 around the origin at y=0:
  1. A BoxGeometry(1.5, 1.5, 1.5) with MeshStandardMaterial color #e94560
  2. A SphereGeometry(1, 32, 32) with MeshStandardMaterial color #0f3460
  3. A ConeGeometry(0.8, 2, 16) with MeshStandardMaterial color #16c79a
  4. A TorusGeometry(0.7, 0.3, 16, 32) with MeshStandardMaterial color #f5a623
  5. A CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.6, 2, 16) with MeshStandardMaterial color #8b5cf6
- Each object should slowly rotate around its own Y axis at a unique speed (0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.4, 0.6 rad/s respectively).

## Wireframe Overlay System
- For each solid mesh, create a corresponding wireframe overlay using EdgesGeometry and LineSegments with LineBasicMaterial.
- Wireframe overlays start HIDDEN (visible = false).
- Wireframe line color should be white (#ffffff) with initial opacity 1.0.
- When a wireframe is toggled ON, it must be rendered with depthTest enabled (material.depthTest = true) so edges behind the solid mesh are properly occluded.
- Provide a button labeled 'Toggle Depth Test' (id='toggleDepthBtn') that toggles depthTest on ALL visible wireframes between true and false. When depthTest is false, all edges render on top (x-ray mode).

## Scoring System
- Maintain a score starting at 0.
- Each time a user toggles a wireframe ON for an object, add 10 points.
- Each time a user toggles a wireframe OFF, subtract 5 points (minimum score is 0).
- Each time the user toggles depth test mode, add 3 points.
- Each time the user cycles wireframe color, add 2 points.
- Display the score in a HUD element (id='scoreDisplay') at top-right corner, styled with white text, font-size 24px, showing 'Score: {N}'.

## Interaction
- Clicking on a 3D object (via Raycaster) toggles its wireframe overlay visibility ON/OFF.
- Keyboard 'W' key: toggles ALL wireframes ON if any are OFF, or ALL OFF if all are ON.
- Keyboard 'C' key: cycles wireframe color through [#ffffff, #ff0000, #00ff00, #0000ff, #ffff00]. All wireframes share the same color. Track the current color index.
- Keyboard 'D' key: same as clicking the 'Toggle Depth Test' button.
- Keyboard 'R' key: resets the entire scene — all wireframes hidden, score reset to 0, color index reset to 0, depthTest reset to true, rotation speeds reset.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- A top-left panel (id='infoPanel') showing:
  - 'Wireframes Active: {count}/5'
  - 'Depth Test: ON/OFF'
  - 'Wire Color: {hex}'
- The score display at top-right (id='scoreDisplay').
- The 'Toggle Depth Test' button (id='toggleDepthBtn') at bottom-center.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- objectCount: number of solid meshes (always 5)
- wireframeVisibleCount: number of currently visible wireframes (0-5)
- wireframeColors: current hex color string of wireframes (e.g. '#ffffff')
- depthTestEnabled: boolean, current depthTest state
- score: current score number
- colorIndex: current index in the color cycle array (0-4)
- allWireframesOn: boolean, true if all 5 wireframes are visible
- allWireframesOff: boolean, true if all 5 wireframes are hidden
- objectRotations: array of 5 numbers, current Y rotation of each object in radians
- cameraDistance: distance from camera to origin
- lastToggledIndex: index (0-4) of the last individually toggled object, or -1 if none
- resetCount: number of times reset has been triggered (starts at 0)
physics_constraints: Rotation speeds must remain constant per object. Score must never go below 0. Wireframe count must always be in [0,5]. Color index must cycle modulo 5. Camera distance must be a finite positive number.
